newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices up 1/4 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices up 1/4 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up about 1/4 point in moderate midday trade, lagging the U.S. government market where the 30-year benchmark was up 3/4 of a point.
"They're definitely up," a municipal trader said. "(It's) a little bit active, we've had some trades in here today."
He credited thin supply with helping to boost prices.
"There's too few municipal bonds around, it's a very, very thin market," the trader said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 23/33 at 97-16/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
"There's an Asian central bank buyer of 10-year notes, that's one," a trader said. "Number two, there was a large buyer of bonds showing up..."
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 29/32 at 117-5/32. The September T-bond contract was up 27/32 at 110-27/32. The MOB spread was 202 ticks.

Municipal bonds are currently rich versus Treasuries, and a municipal trader expects that relationship to continue. As of Thursday's close, 30-year triple-A municipal securities were yielding 79.9 percent of comparable Treasuries.
"I think in the absence of supply, which it doesn't look like we are going to get much, I think we should maintain these spreads," he said.

Next week, however, is shaping up to be a big one for new supply with $4.8 billion of fresh debt expected. It should be the largest weekly total so far in 1997, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $2.7 billion in 63 sales, with a $540 million Puerto Rico Public Building Authority deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the list.
